question: Two circles touch each other externally at T. RS is a direct common tangent to the two circles touching the circles at P and Q. ∠TPQ = 42°. ∠PQT (in degrees) is:
solution:
**Given:**

∠TPQ = 42°

**Concept used:**

The sum of all three angles of a triangle = 180°

The sum of all angles on a straight line = 180°

**Calculation:**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e5e7806c2e7699506c1da9551fd022b9fc6f681405b47b2224853247eda2e622.png] **

Draw a tangent to the circles at T, intersecting QP

So, OT and OQ are two tangents to a common circle from the same external point O

Therefore, OQ = OT then ∠OQT = ∠OTQ

Also, OT and OP are two tangents to a common circle from the same external point O

Therefore, OP = OT then ∠OPT = ∠OTP

∠TPQ = 42°

Then, ∠TPQ = ∠OPT = ∠OTP = 42°

In ΔOPT, ∠OPT + ∠OTP + ∠POT = 180°

⇒ 42° + 42° + ∠POT = 180°

⇒ ∠POT = 180° - 42° - 42° = 96°

Also, ∠POT + ∠QOT = 180°

⇒ 96° + ∠QOT = 180°

⇒ ∠QOT = 180° - 96° = 84°

In ΔQOT, ∠OQT + ∠OTQ + ∠QOT = 180°

⇒ ∠OQT + ∠OQT + 84° = 180° [∵ ∠OQT = ∠OTQ]

⇒ 2 ∠OQT = 180° - 84°

⇒ 2 ∠PQT = 96°

⇒ ∠PQT = 96°/2 = 48°

**∴ The value of ∠PQT (in degrees) is 48°**
